answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the ivory ledger and pays a copper tax each epoch: the first pays 35, the k-th pays 35+5(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 5,030. A karst auditor recomputes every receipt against the public karst tax table at epoch close; a reused copper token or unpaid tax burns the bond. Forging 1,000 identities costs 2,532,500 in tax plus 70,000 bonded against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 35 once and keeps its full share.
